subsystems.name: Collector swarm
subsystems.role: intercepts starlight and turns it into usable power.

subsystems.name: Power distribution
subsystems.role: moves energy from collectors to wherever the work is happening.

subsystems.name: In-space manufacturing base
subsystems.role: turns asteroid and moon material into new collectors, so the structure can grow itself.

subsystems.name: Star-lifting rig
subsystems.role: extracts matter from the star itself to extend its life and supply raw material.
parts: coils generating magnetic fields comparable to the star's own
collection orbits for the extracted material

subsystems.name: Thermal management
subsystems.role: radiates the waste heat that any real structure must shed — and which is the only way we could detect one.

subsystems.name: Coordination network
subsystems.role: keeps trillions of independent objects from colliding.

buildSteps.title: Survey the target system
buildSteps.detail: Map asteroids, moons and comets, since all construction material has to come from outside the star.

buildSteps.title: Bootstrap a first factory
buildSteps.detail: Land automated mining and refining equipment on a small body and use solar power to make more machines from the material already there.

buildSteps.title: Grow exponentially
buildSteps.detail: Each generation of machines builds the next, roughly doubling collector area every replication cycle — the same logic already used on a small scale in robotic manufacturing.

buildSteps.title: Deploy the first ring
buildSteps.detail: Collectors are placed in carefully chosen non-crossing orbits so the swarm is stable for centuries.

buildSteps.title: Scale toward a partial sphere
buildSteps.detail: Coverage grows until a significant fraction of the star's light is intercepted; waste heat then shifts the star's output into the infrared.

buildSteps.title: Build magnetic lifting coils
buildSteps.detail: For star lifting, enormous magnetic structures are built close to the star to grip and channel its outer plasma into collection orbits. This is pure theory — no material or magnet of this scale is known to be feasible.

buildSteps.title: Radiate waste heat
buildSteps.detail: Radiators held clear of the collectors dump absorbed energy at low temperature, otherwise the structure cooks itself.

buildSteps.title: Operate for geological time
buildSteps.detail: Replace worn collectors, manage orbital drift and collisions, and maintain the field that keeps lifted plasma under control.

prerequisites.why: nothing remotely comparable exists; without self-copying machines the required mass could never be launched.

prerequisites.tech: Low-cost access to and mining of asteroids
prerequisites.why: sample return and early resource-extraction demonstrations exist, but only at kilogram scale.

prerequisites.tech: Heat-resistant materials for the inner swarm
prerequisites.why: collectors close to a star must survive intense radiation and thermal cycling.
beamed-power links have been demonstrated over kilometres, not astronomical distances.
tokamaks hold hot plasma in a laboratory; holding a star's surface plasma is a different order of problem entirely.
the relevant orbital mechanics is understood, though never exercised at this scale.

pathway.milestone: robotic mining and in-space manufacturing demonstrations on the Moon and small bodies
pathway.unlocks: the ability to build structures from material that was never launched from Earth.

pathway.milestone: kilometre-scale solar arrays assembled and powered in orbit
pathway.unlocks: megawatt-to-gigawatt power in space, a prerequisite for anything larger.

pathway.milestone: automated factories that build copies of themselves from asteroid material
pathway.unlocks: exponential growth of installed collector area without exponential launch costs.

pathway.milestone: a measurable infrared excess around a star — the classic Dyson-sphere signature, for which surveys have so far found no confirmed candidate
pathway.unlocks: a partial swarm capturing a meaningful fraction of stellar output.

pathway.milestone: star lifting to slow a star's evolution and supply matter to the swarm
pathway.unlocks: a system that can be sustained for far longer than a normal stellar lifetime — entirely theoretical.
